decisions.reason: Although later website visibility is weak, this illuminated candle arch still builds mainly on the firm's core candle-arch craftsmanship and can be adapted through internal workshop learning without much new external knowledge.

The one-tier Christmas pyramid is very close to the firm's established competence base, so absorptive capacity is high and management would usually retain such a product unless it clearly underperformed.

The electronic music box remains technologically distant from the firm's traditional craft knowledge, and with no later market visibility and limited sectoral R&D depth, the firm is unlikely to keep investing in learning this platform.
This accessory depends on the same distant electronic product architecture as Product C, so its weak standalone fit with the firm's knowledge base makes withdrawal highly likely.

The Dresden-themed Christmas pyramid uses the firm's familiar pyramid design and decorative capabilities, so despite uncertain visibility it still fits the existing assortment better than more distant experiments.
